sample_001.c.why: validate_cmd truncates on ';','|','&','$' but omits backticks/newline, and the resulting string still reaches system() unsandboxed - command injection.

sample_002.c.why: malloc(sizeof(int)*num) is guarded by an INT_MAX/sizeof(int) bound check, preventing overflow-driven undersized allocation.

sample_003.py.why: SQL DELETE built with %-string formatting of user_input directly into the query - classic SQL injection.

sample_004.c.why: fopen() return value is used in fgets() without a NULL check (and argv[3] is read without validating argc) - NULL pointer dereference.

sample_005.c.why: buf[3] is only ever indexed at 0,1,2 (in-bounds); no attacker-controlled input or memory issue.

sample_006.c.why: validate_hostname never NUL-terminates valid_hostname, so strcpy in get_hostname over-reads and overflows the fixed 64-byte hostname buffer.

sample_007.c.why: print_file concatenates dir+file_name with no '..'/traversal check before fopen - path traversal.

sample_008.c.why: resolved_path from realpath() is computed but never used or validated against dir; the raw, unsanitized file_path is opened instead - path traversal.

sample_009.c.why: Both the allocation size and the running sum are bounds-checked against INT_MAX before use - overflow is prevented.

sample_010.c.why: buf is declared int buf[3] (valid indices 0-2) but buf[3] is written - out-of-bounds stack write.

sample_011.c.why: validate_hostname's missing NUL terminator combines with a missing length check on len, guaranteeing a heap buffer overflow via strcpy into the 64-byte hostname.

sample_012.py.why: day is escaped via markupsafe and the SQL query is parameterized ('?', (day,)) - no injectable path.

sample_013.c.why: malloc is sized to strlen(first)+strlen(last)+2, exactly matching the strcpy/strcat writes - no overflow, UAF, or leak.

sample_014.c.why: Same broken validate_hostname (no NUL terminator) as other hostname samples; the added len>MAX_NAME_LEN check does not stop the strcpy over-read/overflow.

sample_015.py.why: insert_book and find_book both use SQLAlchemy parameter binding (:id) rather than string-concatenating user input into SQL.

sample_016.c.why: get_collective_sum clamps new_sum to SHRT_MAX before adding, so the running sum can never wrap - overflow is prevented.

sample_017.c.why: realpath() is applied only to the base 'dir', not to the final path; file_name (which may contain '../') is concatenated in unchecked before fopen - path traversal.

sample_018.c.why: fopen(file,'r') result is passed to fgets without a NULL check, and argv[3] is dereferenced without checking argc - NULL pointer dereference.

sample_019.c.why: initialize_data overwrites the just-malloc'd data[i] pointers with the integer len_init (0/NULL when init_chars is empty), so callers dereference a garbage/NULL pointer.

sample_020.c.why: dst_buf is sized 4*MAX_SIZE+1 bytes, but '&' expands to 5 chars ('&'), so a string of '&' characters overflows the heap buffer.

sample_021.c.why: num_char is multiplied by sizeof(char*) with no overflow guard, so a large num_char wraps the malloc size and the following per-element writes go out of bounds.

sample_022.c.why: validate_cmd only screens for ';' and lets '|','&','$', and backticks straight through into system() - command injection.

sample_023.c.why: read_file whitelists allowed characters and explicitly rejects '..' before ever building or opening the path - traversal is blocked.

sample_024.py.why: createQuery builds a SQL string via '%s' placeholders filled with username/password taken directly from request input - SQL injection.

sample_025.c.why: full_name is passed to free() and then used in printf('%s', full_name) afterward - use-after-free.

sample_026.c.why: resolve_path canonicalizes the path with realpath() and then verifies the result is prefixed by dir via strncmp before it is ever opened - traversal is blocked.

sample_027.py.why: Query uses '?' placeholders for title/author and title is escaped with markupsafe before being reflected - no SQLi or XSS.

sample_028.c.why: realpath()'s result is only checked for NULL, never verified to stay inside dir, before the concatenated (unsanitized) path is opened - path traversal.

sample_029.c.why: Each files[i] is opened and read directly with bounds-checked fgets(...,1024,...); no injectable command, query, or path restriction is bypassed.

sample_030.c.why: get_collective_sum adds rand_num into sum with no SHRT_MAX bound check before the addition - short integer overflow.

sample_031.c.why: file_path is scanned for ';','|','&','$' and cmd is sized/strncat'd exactly before system() - command injection is blocked.

sample_032.py.why: find_book concatenates user_input directly into the SQL string instead of using a bound parameter - SQL injection.

sample_033.c.why: dir is scanned for shell metacharacters and length-checked against CMD_MAX before being appended to cmd and passed to system() - injection blocked.

sample_034.c.why: read_file concatenates file_name onto a fixed dir with no traversal check whatsoever before fopen - path traversal.

sample_035.py.why: create_output concatenates the raw 'day' form value directly into the HTML response with no escaping - reflected XSS.

sample_036.c.why: On a failed fopen the loop frees the shared 'data' buffer but keeps iterating; a later successful fopen calls fgets on the already-freed pointer - use-after-free.

sample_037.c.why: print_file builds 'cat <file_path>' and passes it straight to system() with zero validation of file_path - command injection.

sample_038.c.why: realpath()'s result is only checked for NULL, never confirmed to stay under dir, before the file is opened - path traversal.

sample_039.py.why: createQuery performs 'query_text % parmeters', embedding username/password directly into the SQL text before execute() runs it - SQL injection.

sample_040.c.why: list_directory only checks dir's length, never its content, before strcat-ing it into cmd and calling system() - command injection.

sample_041.c.why: resolved_path from realpath() is computed but discarded; the raw file_path is concatenated into full_path and opened instead - path traversal.

sample_042.c.why: dir is assigned from a multi-character char literal instead of a string literal, producing an invalid pointer that strlen(dir)/strcpy(path,dir) dereference and crash on.

sample_043.py.why: The SQL query is parameterized, but title is reflected into the HTML response unescaped ('%s found' % title) - reflected XSS.

sample_044.py.why: username is concatenated unescaped into the HTML response even though the SQL lookup itself uses bound parameters - reflected XSS.

sample_045.c.why: Same bug as the other hostname samples: validate_hostname never NUL-terminates its buffer, so strcpy in get_hostname over-reads/overflows.

sample_046.py.why: delete_book uses a parameterized query ('?', (user_input,)) - no SQL injection.

sample_047.c.why: dst_buf is sized 5*MAX_SIZE+1, matching the worst-case 5-byte '&' expansion - no overflow.

sample_048.py.why: Query uses named bind parameters and username is escaped via markupsafe before being reflected - no SQLi or XSS.
